title: WorldRecipe
description: The versioned contract produced by the AI backend and consumed by Unity. AI decides WHAT the world should be; Unity decides HOW to build it. See docs/world-recipe.md for field-by-field documentation.

version.description: Schema version. Bump on breaking changes. Consumers should warn (not crash) on an unrecognized version.

seed.description: Master seed for deterministic generation. All procedural systems must derive their randomness from this value (see WorldRandom.DeriveSeed). Capped at 2^31-1: Unity reads it into a signed 32-bit int.

theme.description: Free-text theme label used for display/logging (e.g. 'tropical beach'). Not used for asset lookups; terrain/weather/time_of_day are.

sky.description: Selected race-sky presentation from the upload screen.

length.description: Approximate total loop length in meters.

difficulty.description: Normalized difficulty, controls how much the loop curvature is perturbed.

objects.description: Environment decoration types and their relative density. `type` is the label the vision model gave the object it extracted from the source image (snake_case, e.g. 'palm_tree'); it is not a fixed vocabulary. Bootstrap scope: decoration only, never obstacles/hazards.

placement.description: How Unity should use this object, as judged by the vision model that saw the photo. 'landmark': the visual centrepiece (at most one per recipe) -- placed once or twice, oversized, at key points of the track. 'roadside': lines the road at intervals (lamp posts, fences, bollards). 'background': large distant skyline shapes (mountains, towers). 'scattered': natural clutter in groups (rocks, bushes, trees). Optional; absent means 'scattered'. Added backwards-compatibly (version stays 1).

asset.description: Optional handle to an asynchronously generated 3D mesh for this object type. Unity polls GET /assets/{task_id} and swaps the GLB in over its placeholder when ready. Absent/null when no mesh was requested (mock provider, offline fallback) or the submit failed -- Unity then keeps the primitive placeholder.

palette.description: Ordered list of hex colors Unity applies to lighting/ground/skybox placeholders.
